description.narrative: Sida's Core-support to KCSF, Kosovar Civil Society Foundation, will contribute to the organization's goal of a meaningful and sustainable engagement of civil society in socio-economic development processes that serve the public good. The vision with KCSF-s work is to see Kosovo as a prosperous, inclusive and democratic society with an advanced process of EU integration. The support will enable KCSF to work both with policies and research for input to for example the government, and with other non-governmental organizations in supporting them with their own operations in order to contribute and push for a democratic development. The support from Sweden also enables KCSF to forwarding funds through the Pool Funding Mechanism EJA (Engagement for joint action) to small and medium sized organization in the country.

Sidas kärnstöd 2024-2028, till KCSF, Kosovar Civil Society Foundation, ska bidra till organisationens mål om ett meningsfullt och hållbart engagemang från civilsamhället i socioekonomiska utvecklingsprocesser som tjänar medborgarnas bästa. Visionen med KCSF:s arbete är att se Kosovo som ett välmående, inkluderande och demokratiskt samhälle med en avancerad process för EU-integration. Stödet ska göra det möjligt för KCSF att arbeta både med policys och forskning för input till exempelvis regeringen, och med andra icke-statliga organisationer för att stödja dem med sin egen verksamhet för att bidra och driva på en demokratisk utveckling. Stödet från Sverige gör det också möjligt för KCSF att vidarebefordra medel genom Pool Funding Mechanism EJA (Engagemang för gemensamma åtgärder) till små och medelstora organisationer i landet.

The partner, KCSF, has presented a five level Theory of change, with the Vision on the top, followed by Strategic goal/mission, Medium Term objectives, intermediate objectives and then the KCSF functions.
The vision of the work KCSF is "Kosovo is a prosperous, inclusive, and democratic society with an advanced process of EU integration". The vision is then linked to the strategic goal for KCSF to engage the civil society in a meaningful and sustainable way, in socio-economic development processes that serve the public good.
To reach the strategic goal KCSF will, as part of the medium term objectives, build capacity of civil society organizations - such as enhancing their knowledge, support them with diverse resources (also grants), connecting them to different actors and offering platforms and coordination. KCSF's work to improve the legal framework on a government level is also part of this medium term objective with the strive for civil society to be part of public processes and strengthening new laws and so forth.
The medium term objectives can only be reached if also new actors (new partners for KCSF) are engaged. Therefore, for the new core-phase, KCSF has added intermediate objectives to their theory of change, meaning outreach and cooperation with private sector and diaspora to make them more engaged in the civil society development in Kosovo. On this level KCSF will also reach out to more civil servants and politicians in order to enhance their knowledge about legal aspects and willingness to engage meaningful with civil society.
All these levels will be reached through KCSF's hands-on work and functions; such as mobilizing and providing adequate financial resources, strengthening capacity to enable a participatory civil society engagement and continuing cooperating with already engaged partners, and new different actors, in the improvement and development of the system for civil society to act.
During the new phase of core-support - until 2028 - KCSF foresee a strengthened civil society, incorporating new actors within the private sector and with the diaspora.

title.narrative: Grant agrement between Sida and Kosovar Civil Society Foundation
Decision on Contribution - Core support to Kosovar Civil Society Foundation 2024-2028

description.narrative:
INTRO
Kosovar Civil Society Foundation, KCSF, is assessed by Sida as a trustful partner which Sida has supported since 2015 with the total sum 60 MSEK (75 MSEK until 2028). The current support is a core support of 31 MSEK (2024-2028).
It is one of the biggest organizations in Kosovo established 1998. It is an independent organization that supports the development of civil society and initiatives that promote a democratic culture and respond to the socio-economic needs of Kosovo, with a particular focus on contributing to the integration process in the European Union. KCSF has 24 persons working full-time. It is registered as a non-governmental organization, NGO, as a foundation as per the Law on Freedom of Association in NGOs in Kosovo.
KCSF supports other organizations with direct support, competence development through a resource center and with grants in different forms (urgent, projects, institutional grants and for networking national and abroad - see below*). The resource center is supported by EU and Sida. The grant-mechanism EJA (Engagement for Joint Action) is supported by Sida and SDC (some years they also had money from the government of Luxembourg). USAID was supporting a program involving the Diaspora and private sector: Civic Engagement Activity, CEA, which has been stopped by the American government.
Results
Since the start of the support KCSF has strengthened its capacity, both regarding its own organization as well as regarding the support given to other smaller civil society organizations.
KCSF has coordinated and also conducted own important research and advocacy work on civil society space, sometimes with Civikos as the relevant umbrella organization for CSOs in Kosovo.
KCSF has during the years made a positive contribution to that CSO's have been able to engage in policy processes. According to the latest evaluation, conducted between mid-April and 20th of June 2023 by Tana Copenhagen, KCSF has successfully lobbied for that government institutions, both at central and local levels, have increased participation of citizens, which has contributed to a more democratic society in Kosovo.
Advocacy efforts were in focus of KCSFs work last year, securing key policy wins such as the removal of NGOs from the list of reporting entities for anti-terrorism purposes (see statement on the annual report of 2024). And as expressed by KCSF the efforts resulted in blocking the problematic Draft Law on Municipal Property, and contributing to NGO risk assessment, policy framework on volunteering, and legal framework to numerous areas related to financial services for CSOs.
Efforts were also resulting in advancing the dialogue on private sector and Diaspora engagement in strategic philanthropy - which has been new areas since the beginning of the new phase of the core support (from January 2024).
KCSF has also led regional advocacy efforts, challenging Kosovos exclusion from the European Economic and Social Committees (EESC), thanks to its own expertise, and leadership, on civic space for the Balkan Civil Society Development Network (BCSDN).
Thanks to the core support KCSF also has been able to continuously develop and structure their internal work in a clear organized way reflecting Human Resources, Finance and IT, Research and advocacy, Capacity development for other organizations, Grant-mechanism EJA and Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E). The last part has been a strong component during the 2024 in their organization's development and special steps for a more secured IT-system has also been taken.
Through its EJA Kosovo program, over one million Euro in grants were allocated to CSOs in the end of 2024, to grassroots initiatives, and activists, ensuring the continued expansion and sustainability of civic engagement and participatory practices in civil society.
A special ceremony was held, as earlier years, for the Democracy Award in Ferizaj. It is worth mentioning this award as the ceremony manifests the importance of drivers for change - for a more democratic society.
The last year the award was given to Enver Kosumi, based on his 20 years of activism in advocating for people with disabilities. Particularly, in 2024, he initiated the establishment of the first day care center for people with disabilities in Ferizaj. This center will provide a safe space and essential services for this marginalized and often neglected community, thus making a direct contribution to improving the well-being of people with disabilities and their families. Kosumi and his team has managed to secure financial support from the municipality, private persons and community in Ferizaj, the Diaspora, and local businesses.
During last year KCSF has worked hard on improving the grant-making systems for EJA, expanding financial and technical support to wider civil society. There is a stable independent organisation around the grants, with a jury interviewing short listed NGOs who applied for support (the interviews are broadcast on social media, aiming for full transparency in the end of the process).
Examples of result from the EJA-support are mostly obvious from the years before 2024. During last year the system was changed, so there are not many results yet from the organizations that received support in late autumn 2024. However, earlier Sida has assessed that there are interesting results in the areas of supporting persons with disabilities (for instance one organisation - KOMF - gathered other smaller organizations for input to a new law), services have been given to persons who mostly need it at the same time as the civil society pushes the government to invest more in the area. Other results reflects more policies in the universities regarding sexual harassment, women's empowerment in businesses, more public spaces, better education and improvement of the environment on a local level.
During the coming time, KCSF will try to increase more engagement for philanthropy ecosystem - supporting civil society.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
